desc: Makes pultruded and pull-wound composite profiles and tubes, including carbon-fibre parts, for wind, industrial and transport customers.
markets: Europe, North America, China and India production; wind energy, buildings, transport and industrial OEM customers.
rationale: Carbon-fibre composite maker could showcase lightweight engineering credibility and host industrial OEM buyers through a technical supplier-style partnership.

desc: Precision-machines turbine blades and critical rotating components for aerospace, defence, power and oil-and-gas engine makers.
markets: Exports most output to global OEMs in Europe, the US and Japan from manufacturing in Hyderabad.
rationale: Precision engineering supplier could use F1 hospitality to court global aerospace and energy OEM buyers and signal Indian manufacturing quality.

desc: Korean maker of polynucleotide-based aesthetic injectables and skincare, best known for the Rejuran skin-booster brand.
markets: South Korea core; exports Rejuran products to Asia and other markets, with skincare sold to inbound tourists.
rationale: Rejuran is a premium aesthetics brand seeking global awareness; F1 lifestyle audiences in Asia and the Middle East suit brand building.

desc: Chinese maker of small home appliances such as vacuums, humidifiers and cleaning devices sold under the Deerma brand.
markets: Mainly China via e-commerce; also sells online in some overseas markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: A value appliance brand building recognition abroad could use F1 digital content, though budget and premium fit are limited.

desc: Taiwanese operator and franchisor of the Chatime bubble tea chain, with stores across many countries.
markets: Taiwan, Southeast Asia, Australia, Canada, the UK and other markets through master franchisees.
rationale: A global bubble tea franchise brand could use F1 race markets such as Australia, Canada and Asia for youth-focused activation.

desc: Japanese startup making large lithium-ion battery storage systems and developing battery-carrying ships for power transmission.
markets: Mainly Japanese utilities and businesses buying grid and commercial energy storage. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Battery technology storyline fits F1 hybrid and sustainability themes; Suzuka hospitality could support B2B sales to Japanese energy buyers.

desc: Develops and sells ultrasound-based aesthetic devices used by clinics for non-invasive skin lifting and tightening.
markets: United States is the main market, plus distributors in Asia, Europe and other regions.
rationale: Aesthetics device brand reaching affluent consumers via clinics; limited direct fit, though Miami or Las Vegas hospitality could engage practitioners.

desc: Provides cross-border payments and foreign exchange into emerging-market currencies for banks, NGOs, development agencies and companies.
markets: Clients worldwide paying into Africa, Asia and Latin America; strong in African currency corridors.
rationale: B2B payments firm could use F1 hospitality to meet banks and multinationals, though brand awareness is not its core need.

desc: Provides airport ground handling, cargo and warehouse services for airlines in Turkey and abroad.
markets: Turkey, Hungary, India, Germany and other airport operations serving international airlines.
rationale: Aviation services group could host airline customers at races, but its B2B niche gives limited reason for a full F1 deal.

desc: Pan-African commercial bank providing retail, corporate and transaction banking across Africa and in financial centres abroad.
markets: About twenty African countries plus the US, UK, France and UAE.
rationale: Pan-African bank building its brand with corporate clients; F1 hospitality could serve elite customers, though Africa currently hosts no race.

desc: Makes body composition analysers and health measurement devices used by gyms, clinics, sports teams and consumers.
markets: South Korea, US, Japan, China, Europe and other markets through subsidiaries and distributors.
rationale: Body composition data suits driver fitness storytelling; a performance-science tie-in could raise awareness among gyms and fitness consumers.

desc: Runs a mobile payments network letting consumers pay for digital services through carrier billing and local wallets.
markets: Merchants such as app stores and streaming services, with consumers paying across many countries.
rationale: B2B payments network could host big-tech merchant clients at races; limited consumer brand need reduces motivation.

desc: Produces carbon-carbon composite aircraft brakes, powder-metallurgy materials and cemented carbides for aviation and industry.
markets: Chinese aviation, defence-related and industrial customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Carbon brake materials have a technical F1 parallel, but domestic, defence-linked customers give little commercial reason to sponsor.

desc: Taiwanese maker of dash cams, vehicle video and navigation devices sold under brands such as Mio.
markets: Taiwan, Europe, Australia and other markets for consumer and fleet in-vehicle devices.
rationale: Driving-camera brand has a natural motoring angle for car-enthusiast audiences in F1 markets such as Europe and Australia.

desc: Designs embedded computing boards, industrial PCs and edge AI systems for automation, transport, medical and defence uses.
markets: Industrial and OEM customers in North America, Europe, Japan, China and Taiwan.
rationale: Edge AI and industrial computing could be showcased in trackside data systems while F1 hospitality courts global OEM customers.

desc: Develops and operates integrated resort towns and residential communities in Egypt, including El Gouna and Makadi Heights.
markets: Egyptian buyers and international holiday-home buyers from Europe and the Gulf.
rationale: Resort developer selling to affluent European and Gulf buyers could use Gulf races for lifestyle marketing, though budgets are modest.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of Orascom Development Holding (SIX-listed)

desc: Sells organic baby food pouches, snacks and kids meals through US grocery and mass retailers.
markets: United States retail and online. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Family-focused US food brand; F1 audiences offer limited fit beyond US races and growing family fanbase.

desc: Makes autonomous mobile robots and software for warehouse goods-to-person picking and logistics automation.
markets: Customers in China, Europe, North America, Japan and other markets, including retailers and logistics firms.
rationale: Warehouse robotics firm expanding globally could showcase automation and host logistics and retail buyers at European and US races.

desc: Manufactures cement and ground granulated blast furnace slag for construction customers across India.
markets: Indian construction and infrastructure markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic cement maker within the JSW group; commodity product and no Indian race give weak motivation.

desc: Develops controllers, software and autonomous mobile robots for factory and warehouse material handling.
markets: Mainly Chinese manufacturers and robot makers, with some overseas customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Robot navigation technology could feature in factory automation storytelling, but a small firm with mainly domestic customers.

desc: Operates and franchises the Auntea Jenny chain of fresh tea and fruit drink shops across China.
markets: Thousands of mostly franchised stores in lower-tier Chinese cities. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Mass-market domestic tea chain; a Shanghai Grand Prix tie-in could reach young Chinese consumers but global fit is weak.

desc: Provides influencer marketing, e-commerce enablement and brand-building platforms for brands and creators across Asia.
markets: Japan, Southeast Asia, Greater China, India and the Middle East through local offices.
rationale: Marketing platform could package F1 creator content for Asian brand clients, but sponsorship as a buyer is a weak fit.

desc: Retailer owning Smiggle stationery and Peter Alexander sleepwear, with stakes in Breville and Myer.
markets: Australia and New Zealand, with Smiggle stores in the UK, Ireland and Asia.
rationale: Kids and sleepwear retail brands have little motorsport fit; the Melbourne Grand Prix offers only local activation.
signals: Apparel brands merged into Myer for a Myer shareholding (January 2025)

desc: Makes professional and defence drones and, through Pix4D, photogrammetry and mapping software.
markets: Defence, security, surveying and inspection customers in Europe, the US and other regions.
rationale: Drone and mapping technology could be showcased in aerial filming or track mapping, though defence focus limits consumer motive.

desc: Provides third-party logistics, warehousing, freight and employee transport services to companies across India.
markets: Indian automotive, consumer, e-commerce and industrial clients. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic contract logistics firm; F1 logistics storyline exists, but customers and operations are India-only.

desc: Makes collaborative robot arms, desktop robots for education and newer humanoid and mobile robots.
markets: China plus customers in Europe, North America and Asia through distributors.
rationale: Cobot maker expanding abroad could stage robot demos in fan zones and showcase automation to manufacturing buyers.

desc: Indian IT services firm offering enterprise applications, digital and engineering services to manufacturing, life sciences and finance clients.
markets: Mainly US clients, plus Europe and India. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Mid-size IT services firm could follow rivals like Cognizant and Mphasis in using F1 hospitality to win enterprise clients.

desc: Sells cybersecurity software and services, including endpoint protection and detection and response, mainly through partners.
markets: Europe, especially the Nordics, with mid-market business customers via partners.
rationale: Cybersecurity is a crowded F1 category; partnership could build European brand awareness against rivals such as CrowdStrike.
flags: being acquired (2025 tender offer; verify status)

desc: Manufactures tyres for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and off-highway vehicles under the TVS Eurogrip brand.
markets: India plus exports to Europe, the Americas and other markets.
rationale: Tyre maker with motorsport credibility could build export brand awareness, but F1 cost is high relative to scale.

desc: Makes lithium iron phosphate battery systems for residential, commercial and telecom energy storage.
markets: Large share of sales to Europe, plus Africa, Australia and Asia.
rationale: Home battery brand selling heavily in Europe could use European races for awareness among installers and homeowners.

desc: Provides IT outsourcing, software development, testing and cloud services to large technology and enterprise clients.
markets: China, United States, Japan and Southeast Asia delivery centres serving multinational clients.
rationale: IT services firm could use F1 hospitality for enterprise clients abroad, though its brand profile is low.

desc: Designs and sells folding bicycles and related products under the Dahon brand worldwide.
markets: China, Europe, North America and Asian markets through dealers and online channels.
rationale: Urban mobility brand could link to race-city commuting and sustainability themes, but budget and fit are limited.

desc: Operates a licensed Hong Kong crypto exchange plus digital-asset investment, tokenisation and infrastructure businesses.
markets: Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, Bermuda and other licensed digital-asset markets.
rationale: Crypto exchanges such as OKX, Kraken and Crypto.com are F1 regulars; a regulated Asian exchange could build credibility similarly.

desc: Makes 3D solder-paste and optical inspection equipment for electronics manufacturing, plus surgical navigation robots.
markets: Electronics manufacturers in China, Southeast Asia, Mexico, Europe and the US.
rationale: Precision 3D measurement technology could feature in engineering storytelling and host electronics manufacturing customers.

desc: Thai hospitality group operating Dusit hotels and resorts, plus education, food and property businesses.
markets: Thailand, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and other markets through managed hotels.
rationale: Hotel brand growing internationally could use Asian and Gulf races for hospitality and guest packages, following Hilton and Hyatt.

desc: Supplies optical networking equipment and transceivers for data centre interconnect, operators and enterprises.
markets: Europe and North America, sold through partners to operators and data centres.
rationale: Optical networking could be pitched around race data transport, but small scale limits a sponsorship case.

desc: Provides AI-driven commerce software for retailers, including conversational search and mobile shopping engagement.
markets: Retail and brand customers in the UK, US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: AI company seeking enterprise credibility could follow AI sponsors in F1 for awareness, retail client hospitality and tech showcase.

desc: Makes car-care products such as waxes, coatings and repair items, plus household and industrial goods.
markets: Japan mainly, with exports of car-care products to Asia and other markets.
rationale: Car-care brand has a natural motorsport fit, as Armor All shows; Suzuka activation could reach Japanese car enthusiasts.

desc: Taiwanese supplier of professional graphics cards, AI computing systems and related solutions based on NVIDIA GPUs.
markets: Taiwan, Asia and Europe enterprise and channel customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: GPU computing reseller has a simulation angle, but limited brand and scale make sponsorship unlikely.

desc: Italian software and IT services group serving aerospace, defence, automotive, banking and industrial clients.
markets: Italy, the UK, Germany, Switzerland and the US, with aerospace training and fintech specialisms.
rationale: Engineering and simulation software could link to F1 technology; Monza and Imola hospitality could serve Italian industrial clients.

desc: Designs and manufactures zinc-based battery systems for long-duration grid and commercial energy storage.
markets: US utilities and developers, with some international projects.
rationale: Non-lithium storage story suits F1 sustainability themes, but the company sells to utilities and is cash-constrained.

desc: Operates AI-powered sidewalk robots that deliver food orders, working with Uber Eats in US cities.
markets: Los Angeles and other US cities, with expansion to Miami and Dallas.
rationale: Robot delivery could create fan-zone novelty at US races, but early revenue limits spend.

desc: Owns and runs trade fair and congress venues in Milan and organises exhibitions and events.
markets: Italian and international exhibitors and visitors, with some events organised abroad.
rationale: Events operator could co-host motorsport fan or business events near Monza, but sponsorship motive is weak.

desc: Makes power electronics such as energy storage converters, EV chargers and power quality equipment.
markets: China plus exports to Europe and other overseas markets.
rationale: EV charging and storage technology fits energy-transition storytelling, though brand ambitions abroad are unclear.

desc: Korean maker of biometric access control, fingerprint and face recognition systems for security and identity.
markets: Korea, Europe, Middle East, Americas and Asia through partners and subsidiaries.
rationale: Biometric access could be showcased in paddock security, with hospitality for enterprise security buyers.

desc: Provides product engineering and embedded software services for semiconductor, automotive, telecom and device companies.
markets: Clients in the US, Europe, Japan and India.
rationale: Automotive embedded software expertise gives a technical link, but scale is small for F1.

desc: Former sports betting technology company that now holds Ether as a treasury strategy for shareholders.
markets: Public-market investors seeking Ethereum exposure. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Crypto treasury firm could use F1 to raise Ethereum brand awareness, but its business is mainly investment holding.
flags: holding / investment vehicle, not an operating brand
signals: Pivoted to Ethereum treasury strategy with private placement led by Consensys (mid-2025)

desc: Provides data analytics, digital operations and customer operations services to banks, telecoms and retailers.
markets: Mainly US and European enterprise clients.
rationale: Analytics services firm could use F1 data storytelling and hospitality to win enterprise clients.

desc: Chinese maker of clear aligner orthodontic systems sold to dentists under the angelalign brand.
markets: China plus expansion into Europe, Brazil, Australia, the US and Asia.
rationale: Aligner brand expanding abroad could use F1 lifestyle reach to build awareness against Invisalign in Europe.

desc: Develops 3D vision cameras and AI software that guide industrial robots in picking and assembly.
markets: China plus customers in Japan, Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: AI vision technology could showcase robotics for factory buyers; limited consumer brand need.

desc: Korean cosmetics company selling skincare and makeup under brands including It's Skin.
markets: South Korea and China, plus other Asian markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: K-beauty brand could use Shanghai and Asian races for awareness, but limited scale reduces motive.

desc: Makes transformer oils, white oils, petroleum jellies and automotive lubricants sold under the Savsol brand.
markets: India plus exports to many countries in Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: Lubricant brands are F1 staples; Savsol could build awareness in export markets, though budget is limited.

desc: Taiwanese brand of memory cards, USB drives, solid-state drives and memory modules sold worldwide.
markets: Consumer retail and online channels in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Storage brand could reach gamers and tech fans via F1 digital content, though budget is small.

desc: Makes microinverters, storage systems and monitoring for residential and commercial solar installations.
markets: Europe, Americas, Australia and emerging markets through installers and distributors.
rationale: Solar brand selling heavily abroad could use European races to raise installer and homeowner awareness.

desc: Greek dairy producer making yoghurt and ice cream, exporting Greek yoghurt to European markets.
markets: Greece plus exports to the UK, Italy and other European countries.
rationale: Food brand with European exports; F1 cost outweighs benefit except possible regional activation.

desc: Brazilian developer and operator of luxury malls, residences, Fasano hotels and a private business aviation airport.
markets: Affluent Brazilian customers, with Fasano hotels abroad. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Luxury real estate and hospitality brand could target wealthy guests at the São Paulo Grand Prix.

desc: Swiss dental company developing peptide-based treatments for enamel regeneration and early caries.
markets: Dental professionals in Europe and the United States. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Early-stage dental technology has little motorsport fit; awareness among dentists is the main need.

desc: Holds rights to the Kappa sportswear brand in mainland China, selling apparel and footwear.
markets: Mainland China retail and online. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Sportswear brand could target young Chinese consumers through the Shanghai Grand Prix, but domestic scope limits fit.

desc: Sells Thai coconut water and coconut drinks under the if and Innococo brands, mainly in Hong Kong and China.
markets: Hong Kong and mainland China, with sales in other Asian markets.
rationale: Healthy hydration brand could tie into athlete themes in Asia, though small budget limits scale.

desc: Japanese maker of electrical discharge machines, machining centres, injection moulding machines and food machinery.
markets: Japan, China, Southeast Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Precision machining tools could be showcased with teams, like Haas and DMG MORI, and host manufacturing customers.

desc: Malaysian operator of Oriental Kopi Hong Kong-style cafes and maker of packaged coffee products.
markets: Malaysia and Singapore, with packaged products exported to other Asian markets.
rationale: Regional cafe brand could activate at the Singapore Grand Prix, though scale is small.

desc: Chinese maker of collaborative and industrial robot arms and motion control systems for manufacturers.
markets: Chinese manufacturers plus some overseas customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Robotics technology could be showcased to manufacturing buyers, but profile and overseas reach are limited.

desc: Operates and franchises the ChaPanda chain of fresh tea drink shops across China and some overseas markets.
markets: Thousands of stores in China, plus South Korea and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Youth-focused tea brand starting abroad could activate at Shanghai and Asian races to build recognition.
